about.title: One chain. One territory. One ambition.
about.copy: Created in 1963, CBG operates the Sangarédi mines and relies on an integrated chain to the port of Kamsar. This platform tells that story through places, teams and published evidence.

journey.title: From mine to world.
journey.lead: Follow the bauxite journey along an integrated logistics chain, from Sangarédi to Kamsar and beyond.

chain.mineDescription: Brought into operation in 1973, the Sangarédi mine is CBG's main extraction site. Ore is mined in an open pit and then sent to the processing facilities.
chain.railDescription: The line connects the Sangarédi mining area with the Kamsar industrial area. CBG presents a 132 km railway infrastructure, also used for community mobility.
chain.kamsarDescription: At Kamsar, ore is received and directed to crushing, drying and quality checks before transfer to the mineral berth.
chain.storageDescription: Strategic stockpiles and quality checks support ore preparation. The sampling tower automatically collects samples before export.
chain.portDescription: The Kamsar port is the final link in the chain. Its mineral berth receives vessels and organizes shipments to international markets.
chain.worldDescription: Prepared bauxite leaves Guinea through the port of Kamsar. Destinations and volumes are available in the official publications.

history.title: More than six decades.
history.copy: Milestones selected from CBG's published timeline, from the company's creation to current operations.
history.creationCopy: Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée was created on 1 October 1963 to develop the bauxite potential of the Boké region.
history.firstShipCopy: The railway was completed in January. Crushing and stockpiling began at Kamsar on 30 April, followed by the first export on 2 August 1973 aboard the Coronia.
history.extensionCopy: The project launched in 2016 strengthened mining, rail and port capacity. The official project page indicates completion in 2024.
history.productionCopy: CBG's published timeline mentions bauxite production of 18,279,755 tonnes in 2024.
history.certificationCopy: CBG announces the continuation of ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications after an AFNOR audit, as well as ASI certification in its official communications.

projects.copy: Projects are shown with their status and source, distinguishing completed work from development announcements.
projects.multiUserCopy: A partnership between ANAIM, CBG, GAC and COBAD for shared railway infrastructure, governed by a Technical Committee and a Users Committee.
projects.extensionCopy: Expansion of mining operations, modernization of rail and port infrastructure, and new stockpiling and processing areas.
projects.refineryCopy: In August 2026, CBG published a new working phase toward making the refinery project a reality. See the source article for current information.
